title: Legacy Chat API Sunset & Migration Playbook for client SDKs
creator: Priya Khanna
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and migration plan for sunsetting the Legacy Chat API endpoints (/v1/legacy/chat and /v1/legacy/stream) and migrating customers to the Consolidated Chat API (/v2/chat). Goals: minimize customer disruption, provide clear migration paths (server SDKs + curl examples), ensure telemetry to detect migration progress and breakages, and coordinate docs, SDK, and console changes.
background_and_rationale: The Legacy Chat endpoints were implemented during our early hosted phase and do not support function/tool calling, structured output hints, or the new authorization header format. Maintaining dual code paths increases runtime complexity, test surface, and delayed rollout of quality improvements. Consolidating to /v2/chat enables a single-surface for streaming, function calling, and structured output guarantees plus improved perf and batching semantics.
migration_guiding_principles: Provide backward-compatible examples for common patterns (simple completion, streaming, tool calling)
Offer SDK helpers and a deprecation shim where feasible to reduce friction
Announce early with a 90-day minimum migration window for active customers
Coordinate with Support and Solutions for high-touch migrations
Instrument and monitor migration signals before enforcement
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation announcement published in Console and Status page with migration checklist
Docs updated with a dedicated migration guide and example diffs for JS/Python/Go SDKs
SDK releases with a compatibility shim that logs a deprecation warning and auto-translates legacy payload fields
Routing layer supports header-based opt-in to strict /v2 behavior to allow staged customer rollout
Telemetry dashboards show 95% of active tokens have requested /v2 chat or used SDK shim within 60 days of GA
No critical customer-reported regressions (P0/P1) attributable to the migration within the first 30 days post-sunset
Automated test coverage for legacy-to-v2 translation logic and end-to-end streaming behavior
migration_steps: Week 0: Internal announcement to GTM, Support, and Eng with migration timeline and runbook
Week 1-3: Publish migration guide, example diffs (JS/Python/Go), and deprecation FAQ
Week 2-6: Ship SDKs (v3.1) with legacy shim that maps /v1 payloads to /v2 and emits usage metrics
Week 4-8: Add runtime routing support to accept legacy endpoints but tag requests as 'legacy_migrated' when shim used
Day 60 after announcement: Begin automated warning header (Deprecation: true) and Console banners for org admins
Day 90 after announcement: Soft block option for trial orgs (configurable, default off) and ramp for free-tier enforcement
Day 120 after announcement: Final sunset date — legacy endpoints return 410 with migration guidance and support contact
Post-sunset (30 days): Extended support window for enterprise customers by request and monitored rollback playbook
monitoring_and_kpis: % of requests to legacy endpoints per org weekly (target < 10% by Day 60)
Number of orgs with >50% traffic still on legacy endpoints (target 0 by Day 90)
Rate of migration-related support tickets (triaged weekly) and P0 regressions count
SDK shim adoption measured by telemetry header 'X-RW-Shim: true'
Latency delta observed for migrated traffic vs legacy baseline
Errors in translation layer (400/500) and streaming mismatch incidents
support_and_govt_handling: Prepare canned migration playbook and migration checklist for Support
Create internal escalation channel with ENG on-call during sunset week
Identify regulated customers (private deployments) and exclude from automatic enforcement unless explicitly agreed
Offer enterprise migration support (paid engagement) and schedule on-prem upgrade notes
rollback_plan: If >5 customer-facing P0s in first 7 days after sunset: immediately re-enable legacy endpoints for affected orgs and open hotfix PR
Maintain a feature-flagged reactivation path in routing to revert 410s within 4 hours
Postmortem and retro with customers and update migration docs based on root cause
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-02-20: Minimum 90-day public migration window agreed by EM, PM, and Legal
Decision 2026-02-25: SDK shim will be best-effort translation; complex function-calling cases require code changes
Trade-off: Shorter sunset reduces maintenance burden but increases customer disruption; chosen 90-day balances runway and cost
Legal requested a documented exception process for government/regulated customers
open_questions: Should we auto-migrate role-based session tokens to the new header format or require manual rotation? (security input needed)
What SLA should we offer enterprise customers for custom migration timelines?
Do we include traffic shaping to prioritize migrated traffic in Dedicated pools during ramp?
